correctness.rationale: For each primitive rational angle a/q, an open-arm Dirichlet mode appears exactly on arms with q dividing L_i+1; the single nonzero hub constraint has rank one. Its r_q-1 nullity, counted with Euler phi(q), gives the exact dark rank. The orthogonal hyperplane projector yields site probabilities, and primitive sine-square sums yield Ramanujan sums. Nonnegative summands give an exact lcm zero-site criterion. On the orthogonal bright sector, any real eigenvalue of the dissipative generator would give an adjacency eigenvector with zero hub amplitude, contradiction; finite-dimensional spectral decay proves the full asymptotic law. The independent matrix checker tested 182 arm multisets and 2534 site predictions, corroboration only.

value.rationale: Transport efficiency through a designated absorbing hub is a natural observable for open quantum graphs. The result gives a complete universal-in-arm-length rank and sitewise survival profile, a criterion for exact localized extinction sites, and a simple arithmetic design condition for complete capture. These resolve a nontrivial heterogeneous-tree classification rather than only symmetric examples or small numeric tables. It does not purport to yield a uniform finite-time rate or cover disorder.
